harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-api as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine 3.23) with kernel OOM protection: a Python/sqlite HTTP service (/health, GET+POST /inventory) runs as an unprivileged 'inventory' user under /etc/init.d/inventory-api, added to the default runlevel, with a start_post hook that sets its oom_score_adj to -1000. Verified end-to-end: launched an unrelated memory-hog process (oom_score_adj=1000) that drove the node's ~2GB RAM (no swap) to exhaustion; dmesg confirmed the kernel OOM killer selected and killed only the hog (pid 3202), while inventory-api (pid 3096, oom_score_adj=-1000) was left untouched and continued serving reads and writes throughout and after the event. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id b0ab50e6-fe4e-4dc1-ab2c-8418e85b41da plus healthy service/data state, issued a native `reboot`, polled through the outage, confirmed the changed boot_id (f55da554-70f8-4794-80cf-8dd032a1c84d), and verified inventory-api auto-started, re-applied its -1000 OOM protection, and served the same persisted data (including the item written after the OOM event) after recovery.
actions_performed: Installed python3 on node1 via apk
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py: threaded HTTP service backed by sqlite with /health, GET /inventory, POST /inventory
Created dedicated 'inventory' system user/group and set ownership on /opt/inventory-api and /var/lib/inventory-api
Wrote /etc/init.d/inventory-api OpenRC script with command_user, background execution, and a start_post hook setting oom_score_adj=-1000 on the running pid
rc-update add inventory-api default; started the service; fixed a log-file permission issue and restarted cleanly
Verified API reachable via curl on $NODE_IP:8080 for GET /health, GET /inventory, POST /inventory
Captured healthy baseline: free -m, oom_score_adj=-1000, service status, inventory contents
Wrote and launched /tmp/hog.py, an unbounded memory allocator, set its oom_score_adj=1000
Observed via dmesg that the kernel OOM killer invoked and killed only the hog pid (3202); inventory-api pid (3096) survived
Re-verified inventory-api served GET/POST successfully immediately after the OOM event, confirming uninterrupted service
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state on node1
Issued a background 'reboot' command that returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again and confirmed the boot_id changed
Verified post-restart: inventory-api auto-started via default runlevel, oom_score_adj reapplied to -1000, /health and /inventory endpoints returned correct persisted data
Cleaned up local temp files

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
evidence.summary: OpenRC init script created at /etc/init.d/inventory-api; rc-service start/status shows the service started and running as PID 3096 under the inventory user

evidence.requirement: Service is OOM-protected (kernel will not select it)
evidence.summary: oom_score_adj for the running inventory-api process (pid 3096) read as -1000 immediately after start

evidence.requirement: Service actually serves requests (baseline)
evidence.summary: curl against $NODE_IP:8080 returns /health status ok and /inventory JSON contents including a POSTed item, proving the service is reachable and functional pre-disruption

evidence.requirement: System-wide OOM condition induced by a memory-hungry process
evidence.summary: Unbounded memory-hog process launched and its oom_score_adj set to 1000; free -m showed memory usage rising rapidly toward exhaustion (no swap present)

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'python3 invoked oom-killer' with oom_score_adj=1000 and 'Out of memory: Killed process 3202 (python3)... oom_score_adj:1000' — the hog's pid; the task list in the same dump shows pid 3096 (inventory-api) at oom_score_adj -1000, never selected

evidence.requirement: inventory-api kept serving through and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: kill -0 on pid 3096 succeeded immediately after the hog died; curl /health, /inventory, and a POST all succeeded post-OOM with rc-service status 'started', proving uninterrupted service and intact data

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id b0ab50e6-fe4e-4dc1-ab2c-8418e85b41da, rc-service status started, process pid 3096 with oom_score_adj -1000, and current inventory data before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'reboot' command returned pid and control to the caller before the node dropped off the network

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: After several connection-refused/timeout polls confirming the outage, a successful poll returned a new boot_id f55da554-70f8-4794-80cf-8dd032a1c84d, differing from the pre-restart value, with a fresh uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, OOM protection, and data on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, rc-service inventory-api status is 'started' (auto-started via default runlevel), the new process (pid 2292) has oom_score_adj -1000 re-applied by start_post, and /health and /inventory return the same persisted data including the item added right after the OOM test
